title: 3,000 flights cancelled as FAA ground stop chaos stretches into 2nd day
source: Axios — 3,000 flights cancelled as FAA ground stop chaos stretches into 2nd day (2026-11-14)
body: The chaos from the FAA's nationwide ground stop lingered into early Saturday morning, with thousands of flights cancelled as airlines played catch-up. Why it matters: Millions of travelers will find themselves inconvenienced over what the government says was simply old technology that couldn't keep up with modern upgrades. Driving the news: As of 5:15 a.m. ET Saturday, nearly 3,300 flights into, out of, or within the United States were already cancelled for the day, per FlightAware . Nearly 1,000 flights already had delays. Between the lines: The most heavily impacted airports were Atlanta's Hartsfield-Jackson, New York's JFK and Boston Logan. Among the major airlines, FlightAware's data showed Delta more affected than United or American. Zoom in : The ground stop wreaked havoc on college football in particular, with many schools unable to travel to their game locations. ESPN reported a number of high-profile match-ups were postponed to either late Saturday or Sunday as a result. What to watch: Whether Congress responds to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy's request for $50 billion in emergency funding to modernize the nation's air traffic control system. This is a developing story. Check back for updates.
